title: Your sangat, chosen
hookLine: name the people you'll remember with
tomorrow: Simran's first paycheck lands. how much is a tenth, really?

cards: They're sitting on the curb outside school, sharing fries, when Maya says it. Different colleges, different states, a whole time zone apart. They've known it for months; it lands anyway.
Simran's been building a list of what to keep, and suddenly the biggest item isn't a prayer or a pantry. It's people. Who will she remember with when Bebe, her dad and Maya are all far away?

teach.b: Sikhs have a word for that: sangat, company, and especially the gathering that sits with the Guru. Guru Nanak gives a test for it on Ang 72, paraphrased: how do you know the true company?

teach.h: ANG 72: WHERE THE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: It's where the One Name is spoken. Not the biggest crowd, not the coolest one. The one where the Name is in the room.
So Simran's first answer is practical: a Sikh student group near campus that sings kirtan on Sundays, and the sangat at home on video when she's homesick. But there's a wider circle too.

Guru Arjan, on Ang 671, says something close to this: I have made everyone my friend, and I am a friend to all. That's the line Simran keeps coming back to on the curb. Maya doesn't pray the way she does.
Maya also sat in the langar row and came back for the dal, told her the speech was good when it wasn't yet, and wouldn't let her back out of giving it. So Simran's list has two parts.
The gathering where the Name is sung. And the friends who keep her true to it. Maya steals her last fry.
That's sangat too, in its way.

how: Sikhs gather as sangat at the gurdwara for kirtan, prayer and langar; students away from home often join a Sikh student group or a nearby gurdwara, and families stay in touch with their sangat at home.

o: the people you choose to remember with, around the Name
a list of relatives who must attend every gurpurab
the seat you're given in the gurdwara hall each week

games.q: sangat, near and far — tap the pairs.
p: true company: where the Name is spoken
a friend who keeps Simran true

s: sangat just means your group of friends
it means company, especially the gathering around the Guru and the Name. friends can keep you true to it.
Guru Arjan wrote that he had made everyone his friend
Ang 671, paraphrased: I have made everyone my friend; I am a friend to all.
Ang 72 says the true company is the biggest one
it says the true company is known where the One Name is spoken.

games.q: first week of college: a group that parties every night, a Sikh student group that sings on Sundays, and a lab partner who studies with you at 7am. who's sangat?
o: the Sunday group where the Name is sung, plus the friends who keep you true.
the biggest group, since a sangat is basically a crowd you belong to.
nobody; a Sikh only needs the Granth, so company doesn't matter much.
games.why: Ang 72 says the true company is where the Name is spoken. Guru Arjan's 'friend to all' widens the circle without changing that test.

practice: Say out loud, quietly, the names of the people you'll remember with: the ones you pray or sing beside, and the ones who keep you honest. Let each name land before you say the next one, and go round again if there's time.

wordCard.voice: Your sangat: the company you choose to remember with, gathered around the Name, and the friends who keep you true.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: company, the gathering of Sikhs around the Guru and the Name.

carryVoice: Your line: my sangat, named out loud, near and far. Two friends on a curb, one fry left.

sources.ref: Ang 72, Sri Rag, Guru Nanak ('satsangat kaisee jaaneeai, jithai eko naam vakhaaneeai'), paraphrased
Ang 671, Dhanasri, Guru Arjan ('sabh ko meet ham aapan keena, ham sabhnaa ke saajan'), paraphrased
